section_1.title: Introduction: The Map-Maker's Challenge
section_1.content: Define a Planar Graph (a graph that can be drawn without edges crossing). Connect this to real-world applications like printed circuit board design or subway map layouts.
section_1.example: Visualize a simple subway map of 3 stations where tracks cross—show how rearranging nodes makes it planar.

section_2.title: Core Components: Vertices, Edges, and Faces
section_2.content: Introduce the anatomy of a planar graph. Define 'Faces' as the enclosed regions, including the infinite 'outer face'. Emphasize that these components are the building blocks of the formula.
section_2.example: A triangle (3 vertices, 3 edges) has 2 faces: the inner triangle and the infinite area surrounding it.

section_3.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
section_3.content: Present the fundamental theorem: V - E + F = 2. Explain that this elegant constant holds true for all connected planar graphs regardless of their complexity.
section_3.example: Use an animation of a square with a diagonal: V=4, E=5, F=3. Calculation: 4 - 5 + 3 = 2.

section_4.title: The Concept of Dual Graphs
section_4.content: Explain how to construct a Dual Graph: create a new vertex inside every face of the original graph and connect them across shared edges. Connect this to symmetry and topological transformations.
section_4.example: An animation showing a hexagon honeycomb grid transforming into a set of connected triangles (the dual).

section_5.title: Summary & Application
section_5.content: Review the relationship: Properties of the original graph (V, E, F) directly dictate the properties of the dual graph (V', E', F'). Conclude with the importance of these tools in graph coloring and network reliability.
section_5.example: Show a circuit diagram being simplified using duality to check for signal interference paths.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(list_obj, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(list_obj))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

from manim import *

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
